description: Maintain player scores as they change, return the sum of the highest k scores, and remove a player's score on reset. Example 1: scores 73, 56, 39, 51, and 4 yield a top-one sum of 73. Example 2: after resetting the 73- and 56-point players and adding 51 points for one of them, the top three sum to 141. Constraints: player IDs are unique while active and requested top counts do not exceed the number of active players.
intuition: A score map supports updates and resets, while sorting active scores answers top-k queries.

brute_force.approach: Store scores in a map and sort every score whenever top(k) is requested.
brute_force.time: addScore O(1), top O(n log n), reset O(1)

optimal.approach: Keep a score map and use a balanced ordered multiset to retrieve the largest k values.
optimal.time: addScore O(log n), top O(k), reset O(log n)

edge_cases: Adding points to an existing player changes rather than replaces the score.
Resetting a player removes that player's complete score.
